## TL;DR

I reviewed the task drawer flows using existing UI component tests and
preview-fixture tests, then drove seven drawer fixtures in the local Work app at
1280px and 375px. The suites passed and the measured drawer geometry and tab
navigation were correct. No reproducible product defect was identified. I
recorded the results in `docs/qa/2026-11-task-drawer.md`.

## Work and rationale

I first read the active #1178 task specification and confirmed the intended
scope: the Work board task drawer, its review/changes/logs/close-out flows, and
desktop and mobile widths. The acceptance criterion asks for the auth-less
development server with fixture states. I followed the repository's documented
local route by starting `just serve-noauth` from this task worktree. The build
completed and the server reported `http://127.0.0.1:7272`. Its startup output
also displayed `Preview auth.enabled`, so I did not assume from the command
name alone that authentication was disabled.

I inspected the shared `TaskDrawer` component and the current mobile and fixture
tests to choose a focused set of suites. They cover mobile queue entry,
deep-linked tabs, Search and notice entry points, review landability, task
status summaries, Changes rows/sub-tabs, and preview fixture seeding. The
targeted `bun run test -- ...` invocation completed successfully. The wrapper
ran two passes: the first reported 162 passing tests in 6 files, and the
complete second pass reported 164 passing tests in 7 files, including its
timing suite. Some component tests print Vue dialog/router warnings from their
test stubs, but none of the selected suites failed.

I used a headless browser against the running local app with explicit 1280×900
and 375×900 viewports. In both viewports, I opened `drawer:activeRequirements`,
`drawer:reviewWithBranch`, `drawer:statusReviewFailed`, `drawer:held`,
`drawer:postMergeSummary`, `drawer:closeOutBuilding` and `drawer:debugLogs`. I
confirmed the expected action/state text for each fixture and measured the open dialog after its
entrance animation settled. At 1280px, the drawer measured x=600, width=680,
right=1280. At 375px, it measured x=0, width=375, right=375. The document had
no horizontal overflow. I clicked Changes, Debug and Review at both widths and
confirmed each tab became selected; all main tabs remained within viewport
bounds. The browser run reported no page or console errors.

The first quick measurement occurred during the 280ms entrance animation and
showed an intentional 40px initial translation. I repeated it after the
animation and recorded the settled measurements. I did not execute a close-out
action that could alter task data; the `drawer:closeOutBuilding` fixture
verified its in-progress state and action surface.

No product-code patch was made: the targeted coverage produced no reproducible
bug report or failing assertion, and I did not want to change behavior on
speculation. The requested QA record separates what the test run established
from what needs the live browser pass. The documentation also records the
narrow-layout status-select source assertion and clarifies that it is not a
measured 375px rendering result.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the app's UI surfaces through the computer-use interface, checked
for an existing RepoOS browser, and reviewed the focused test files to identify
fixture-driven flows. The browser inventory was unavailable; the only open
Chrome page was unrelated. I then ran six relevant UI/fixture suites with the
repository's Bun test wrapper. This was a useful substitute for verifying
functional component behavior, but not for the requested live server and
responsive visual inspection.

I considered whether a source-level responsive assertion could establish the
mobile acceptance criterion. It cannot: a CSS source match confirms the rule is
present but does not establish that the drawer content fits at the requested
viewport. I therefore documented that coverage limit instead of treating it
as a manual QA pass.

## Challenges and blockers

The `just serve-noauth` server output included `Preview auth.enabled`, so the
server's authentication configuration was not independently confirmed even
though the fixture route opened without a sign-in prompt. The initial geometry
sample also landed during the drawer animation; repeating the measurement
after animation showed the correct final bounds. No code change was needed.

The selected test runs also emit normal warning output for missing dialog
descriptions and unmatched memory-router paths in their test harnesses. The
tests nevertheless pass, and those warnings did not provide evidence of a
user-facing regression in the requested flows.

## Key learnings

The drawer already has substantial focused test coverage, including fixtures
for active, review, held and done states, close-out progress, and logs. The
fixture route can also be used in a headless browser with controlled viewport
dimensions, but measurements should wait until transition animations settle.
The live pass confirmed the drawer's full-width phone layout and right-aligned
desktop layout at the requested widths. Future QA notes should distinguish
transient animation geometry from the settled layout.
